Worth the trip.

Places in this region people keep coming back to. Not a ranking — a starting point.

  • Jamestown

    Fishing harbour, boxing gyms and one of Accra's oldest quarters.

    Wikipedia ↗

  • Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park

    Ghana's most visited attraction: the mausoleum and museum of the first president.

    Visit Ghana guide ↗Wikipedia ↗

  • Makola Market

    The city's central market. Cloth, food, and most other things.

    Wikipedia ↗

  • Labadi Beach

    Accra's busiest stretch of sand, liveliest at the weekend.

    Wikipedia ↗

  • Osu

    Food, bars and late-night Accra around Oxford Street.

    Wikipedia ↗

  • Arts Centre for National Culture

    Carving, kente and craft stalls near the sea.

Festivals in
Greater Accra.

Festivals and cultural events kept here, in calendar order. Many dates move from year to year, so each festival’s page has what we know about when.

  • Mar–Apr

    Kpledjoo

    Tema’s festival at the Sakumo lagoon: two days of rites, processions and prayers for fish and food.

    Usually late March or early AprilTema

  • Late Jul–Aug

    Asafotufiam

    Ada’s warriors’ festival: Asafo companies re-enact old battles, with musketry and a durbar of chiefs in palanquins.

    Late July or early August, with the durbar on a SaturdayAda

  • Aug

    Chale Wote

    Accra’s street art festival: murals, performance, music and film in the streets of James Town and beyond.

    Usually August, over about a weekJames Town and Osu, Accra

  • Aug–Sep

    Homowo

    “Hooting at hunger”: kpokpoi is shared and sprinkled for the ancestors.

    August into September, each Ga town in turnAccra and the Ga coast
